## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Enriching TOEFL essay vocabulary with ChatGPT cut the false positive rate from 61.22% to 11.77%, showing detectors key on vocabulary and predictability, not authorship. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2304.02819 · keywords: Consequences for tic lists and detectors · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37521038/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Seven GPT detectors misclassified non-native English TOEFL essays as AI with 61.22% average false positive rate, versus 5.19% on US 8th-grade essays; the mechanism is perplexity, since lower lexical variability reads as machine-like. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2304.02819 · keywords: Consequences for tic lists and detectors · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37521038/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing guide says its signs indicate potential problems, not proof, that it is not a ban on words, and that treating signs as problems to fix could make detection harder. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing · keywords: Consequences for tic lists and detectors
- [statement] Tic vocabulary shifts by model generation (earlier delve/intricate, newer enhance/showcase), so a fixed word list decays and needs dating. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing · keywords: Consequences for tic lists and detectors
- [statement] A 2026 arXiv paper reports that writing style (vocabulary complexity, formality) is a confound causing detector false positives on academic writing, so formal human prose can be flagged. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-28) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.26710 · keywords: Consequences for tic lists and detectors
- [statement] The Nigerian-English explanation for 'delve' is contested: comparing base Llama 2 to its RLHF-tuned version suggests RLHF preference itself promotes such words. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.11385 · keywords: Consequences for tic lists and detectors
